newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Tight bean supplies raise basis.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Tight bean supplies raise basis.

text.p: Tight supplies of soybeans and expected crushing plant downtime next week pushed some rail offers up sharply Friday, U.S. soymeal brokers said.

"It's hard to buy beans right now and it will be for a couple of weeks," said one dealer in the southeast U.S. "There's a lot of bullish sentiment out there, and it has helped run the basis up $4.00 (per ton) this week."
Basis values in deferred months also jumped sharply as end-users buy soymeal to cover needs for this summer.
"We're seeing a little bit of panic buying in June and July (positions)," a broker said.
"In case there isn't any soymeal this summer, you'd better have some on the books," the broker said.

Several large crushers in the Midwest are scheduled to take down-time next week. Cargill's Kansas City crushing plant closed Thursday and will be down through the summer, a spokeswoman confirmed earlier.
The weekly National Oilseed Processors Association crush of 25.043 million bushels came in higher than trade expectations for 24.1 to 24.9 million bushels.
